title.value: Transbronchial Cryobiopsy in Diffuse Parenchymal Lung Disorders

key_points: TBLC is increasingly first-line when histopathology is needed for diffuse parenchymal lung disease.
General anesthesia with airway control is common; bronchial blockers are strongly recommended to prevent/mitigate major bleeding.
Common guiding systems include fluoroscopy; CBCT, CLE, radial EBUS, and OCT are useful in selected cases.
Cryoprobes: 1.1 mm, 1.7 mm, 2.4 mm (length 1150 mm); typical freezing times: 2.4 mm ≈ 6 s; 1.7 mm ≈ 8 s; 1.1 mm ≈ 12–13 s.
Diagnostic yield is ~80% with larger samples than forceps TBB; pneumothorax is the most frequent complication (mean ~5%; range <1–30%).
Relative contraindications include FVC <50% predicted, DLCO <35% predicted, PAPs >40 mmHg, significant emphysema, and recent clinical deterioration; coagulopathy/instability are absolute.

clinical_procedures: Intubate (rigid tracheoscope or endotracheal tube) under general anesthesia; place one or more bronchial blockers.
Advance flexible bronchoscope through the airway device to target segment; pass cryoprobe via working channel.
Under fluoroscopy, touch pleura then withdraw ≈1 cm (probe tip length).
Freeze per probe size (approximate): 2.4 mm ~6 s; 1.7 mm ~8 s; 1.1 mm ~12–13 s; maintain during en bloc withdrawal.
Immediately inflate the pre-positioned blocker to occlude the airway; deflate periodically to reassess; reinflate 3–10 min for bleeding.
Obtain ≥2 segments (same lobe) from most affected areas when feasible; aim for largest diameter >5 mm and pleura in specimen.
Specimen handling: thaw/detach gently and fix promptly; prepare serial slides; reserve unstained slides for special/IHC/molecular tests.
diagnostic_approaches: Primary guidance: fluoroscopy; adjuncts: CBCT, CLE, radial EBUS, OCT as available.
Select targets by CT pattern (avoid central carina-level biopsies; favor peripheral alveolated tissue).
Post-procedure check for pneumothorax (US or CXR within 2–3 h in outpatients if symptomatic or per protocol).
treatment_algorithms: Candidate selection: pursue TBLC when MDD lacks a confident diagnosis after noninvasive testing/BAL and histology is expected to change management.
Airway strategy: general anesthesia + blocker(s); consider spontaneous ventilation where feasible; avoid excessive ventilatory pressures.
Sampling strategy: probe perpendicular to chest wall; distance to pleura ≲10 mm; multiple segments improve yield.
Hemostasis: prophylactic blocker; if bleeding, occlude 3–10 min; consider cold saline or diluted epinephrine; TXA utility uncertain.
Escalation: if TBLC inconclusive, proceed to SLB; staged strategy reduces burden/hospital stay compared with immediate SLB.
clinical_guidelines: Use bronchial blockers prophylactically to reduce major bleeding risk.
Prefer 1.7–2.4 mm probes for DPLD; 1.1 mm may be considered for simpler histologies (e.g., sarcoid, OP) with longer freeze.
Avoid central biopsies and strong ventilator support; keep probe close to pleura under fluoroscopy.

Relative contraindications: FVC <50% predicted, DLCO <35% predicted, PAPs >40 mmHg, significant emphysema, hypoxemia (PaO2 <55–60 mmHg), high BMI with desaturation risk, recent deterioration possibly consistent with AE-IPF.
Absolute contraindications: coagulation defects/thrombocytopenia and hemodynamic instability.

rows.value: Fogarty balloon(s); two if sampling different lobes

definitions.definition: Transbronchial lung cryobiopsy for diffuse parenchymal lung disease.
Cooling effect when compressed gas expands at the probe tip.
Inflatable balloon to occlude airway and control bleeding/pneumothorax risk.
Cone-beam computed tomography; improves localization in limited-extent ILD.
Confocal laser endomicroscopy; identifies septa, pleura, inflammatory/fibrotic areas.
Optical coherence tomography; microscopic assessment, e.g., UIP features.
Usual interstitial pneumonia pattern; TBLC can capture pleura and septa to aid diagnosis.
Acute exacerbation of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

clinical_pearls: Keep the probe close to pleura (≈1 cm withdrawal from pleural touch) to maximize alveolated tissue and reduce bleeding.
Use prophylactic balloon occlusion; re-inflate 3–10 minutes if bleeding occurs and reassess every 2–3 minutes.
Multiple segments (same lobe) and presence of pleura in specimen correlate with higher diagnostic yield.
Avoid strong ventilatory support to reduce barotrauma risk; accept permissive hypoxemia/hypercapnia during sampling.

clinical_applications: Provide histopathology to refine ILD diagnosis and guide therapy where noninvasive data are insufficient.
Enable multidisciplinary diagnosis with high yield while avoiding SLB for many patients.
practice_recommendations: Use blockers prophylactically; target peripheral alveolated lung; sample ≥2 segments.
Adopt fluoroscopy as standard; add advanced guidance for difficult patterns or limited disease.
future_directions: Portable TBLC units; ROSA/AI-enhanced onsite assessment.
controversies: Optimal probe size vs pneumothorax/bleeding balance.
Role of 1.1 mm probe in complex DPLD patterns.

points: TBLC provides large, high-quality parenchymal samples with ~80% yield for DPLD while avoiding SLB in many cases.
Major risks are mitigated by blockers and peripheral targeting; pneumothorax occurs in ~5% on average.
Training, case volume, and standardized protocols improve outcomes and safety.
